extracted.intended_audience: children's book authors and illustrators (especially Latino/Latina creators), librarians, educators, and readers interested in Latino children's literature
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and basic rules for the Pura Belpré Award honoring Latino/Latina authors and illustrators whose work portrays and celebrates the Latino cultural experience in outstanding children's and youth literature. Includes category distinctions (author vs illustrator), award history, and recognition types (winner/honor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary award criterion (portray/affirm/celebrate Latino cultural experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goes to "a Latino/Latina writer and illustrator whose work best portrays, affirms, and celebrates the Latino cultural experience in an outstanding work of literature for children and youth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quoted mission statement is the central evaluative standard: the work should portray, affirm, and celebrate Latino cultural experience and be an outstanding piece of literature for children/youth. This implies considerations of cultural authenticity, positive representation, and overall literary/illustrative quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — creator identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Award goes to "a Latino/Latina writer and illustrator" (i.e., the creator must be Latino/Latina).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement specifies the ethnic/cultural identity of eligible creators (Latino/Latina). The page does not elaborate further on eligibility criteria (e.g., publication dates, language, nationality) beyond this identity requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience — children's and youth literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The work must be "an outstanding work of literature for children and youth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible/award-worthy works are those intended for children and young readers; evaluators therefore consider suitability for those age groups, age-appropriate content, and impact on child/youth audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate award categories — authors and illustrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Like the Coretta Scott King Award, there are awards for both authors and illustrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Pura Belpré Award separately recognizes writing and illustrating. Submissions/consideration and judging happen in distinct author and illustrator categories, with winners and honor books named in each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition types — winner and honor distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists include both Award winners and Honor books (multiple honor books appear in some years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award system distinguishes a single winner per category (in most years) and one or more Honor books that receive formal recognition; selection may result in multiple honors in a category in a given year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award frequency and history
rubrics_metrics.description: The award was established in 1996; it "was first given every two years, so there are no entries for 2007, 2005, or 2003. In 2009, it became an annual award."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cadence of the award has changed (biennial originally, annual since 2009), which affects which publication years are eligible in early cycles; historical gaps reflect the earlier biennial schedule.
